faq.q: What information does each element show?
faq.a: Click any element to see its atomic number, symbol, name, atomic mass, category and metal/nonmetal/metalloid type, period, group, block (s/p/d/f), state at room temperature, density, melting and boiling points, electronegativity, and electron configuration (e.g. [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s² for iron). All 118 elements are included, with lanthanides and actinides shown in their own rows below the main grid.

faq.q: How do I compare two elements?
faq.a: Hold Ctrl (or Cmd on Mac) and click two elements. A comparison table appears showing both side by side across atomic mass, density, melting point, boiling point, electronegativity, state, block and electron configuration. A "Clear Compare" button resets the selection.

faq.q: Can I filter and search the table?
faq.a: Yes. Search by name, symbol or atomic number (e.g. Hydrogen, Fe, or 26). Filter dropdowns narrow the table by category (alkali metal, halogen, noble gas, etc.), by metal/nonmetal/metalloid, by state at room temperature, and by block. Non-matching elements are dimmed rather than hidden. Keyboard shortcuts let you press / to search, arrow keys to move between elements, Enter to open and Esc to close.

faq.q: Can I save elements or copy their data?
faq.a: Yes. Each element's panel has "Copy details" (readable text) and "Copy as CSV row" buttons, plus a Save/star button. Saved elements and a recently-viewed list are kept in your browser's local storage across visits (under periodic-favs-v1 and periodic-recent-v1) and appear as quick-jump chips. Everything runs locally with no server involved.
